answer: What survives to the fable is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Each submission hangs on the beacon of a task receipt, and the vault is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on time-locked work history, reduced by each unverified claim, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name.
